and applying Nature-based Solutions (NbS) with specific application to food and tourism sectors. projects.name: The Parliaments in Niue and Cook Islands are more effective, representative, inclusive, and accessible in their law-making, budget and oversight
projects.description: PPEI 3 builds on previous phases of support in assisting beneficiary parliaments to progress towards being more effective, representative, inclusive, and accessible in their law-making, budget and oversight. To this end, the project will support parliaments in improving their cooperation with their governments, strengthening their legal and procedural basis, improving their committee systems, and developing effective approaches to bill review, budget review, and oversight. It will foster civic engagement, strengthening public participation in the work of parliament. It will continue fostering regional Pacific integration. The project will strengthen parliament’s ability to develop sustainably, to plan and deliver parliamentary services, and to build important knowledge, skills, and abilities of staff and MPs without overreliance on development partner support. The project will help parliaments become more representative of women, persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups, as well as more transparent, accessible and effective in facilitating  public participation. It will work with women, youth, and PWD leaders, activists, and champions inside and outside of parliament to empower their political leadership. The project will also help parliaments engage more effectively with the public and civil society.
projects.outcome: 4.2.1 Strengthened legislative policies of parliaments, electoral systems and constitutional bodies and capacities to provide more inclusive and participatory processes.

projects.description: The Solomon Islands is one of the world’s most environmentally fragile countries, facing severe hydrometeorological and geophysical hazards alongside slow‑onset climate impacts that are intensifying community vulnerability and fragility. projects.name: ASMP Support Mechanism for the Pacific (ASMP)
projects.description:
A Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) for the setup and operations of the ASYCUDA Support Mechanism for the Pacific (ASMP) was signed late 2000 by Customs Administrations of Fiji, Samoa, Vanuatu, which PNG and Solomon Islands joined in 2008 and 2016, respectively. The main objective of this long standing project is the strengthening of technical and functional capacity, with provision for technical assistance to further develop the respective Customs automated systems of the three participating countries.

The ASMP is recognised as an important project as it demonstrates the participating countries’ commitment to the ASYCUDA and the relevance of its programme outputs in ensuring long term sustainability of the reformed and automated processes in the respective Customs administrations.

projects.name: The Parliament in Cook Islands Parliaments is more effective, representative, inclusive, and accessible in their law-making, budget and oversight
projects.description:
Support parliaments in putting in place and maintaining the necessary support and services their MPs require to perform more effectively. The focus will be on training and professional development of MPs and staff, and the planning and delivery of improved services. This will include supporting parliaments to develop and implement their strategic plan based on an understanding of the service needs, the parliament, its work bodies and MPs. This will also include support to integrate business continuity planning to allow parliaments to better deal with emergency situations. The project 
will support parliaments in building capacity of staff, and knowledge and skills of Members in a sustainable manner. PPEI III will support all parliaments to flexibly find solutions in conducting 
capacity-building of staff and professional development of MPs in sustainable ways with less reliance on international partners. This will include building national parliamentary training capacities for essential knowledge and skills, and regional cooperation in training, in particular for MP induction. The project will also explore how pooled resources (as in the FBO) may be used by the parliaments to deliver other specialist parliamentary services at reduced cost. It may also include exploring how parliaments and governments may cooperate in training for the parliamentary and wider civil service. The project will expand its support, commenced in PPEI II to the digitalization of parliaments with a view to improving how parliaments conduct their business in the plenary and committees, how they deliver services, and how they inform and interact with the public. The experience with COVID-19 has shown that digitalization of parliamentary business is also key for business continuity to cope with the 
consequences of future natural or man-made disasters.
projects.outcome: 4.2.1 Strengthened legislative policies of parliaments, electoral systems and constitutional bodies and capacities to provide more inclusive and participatory processes.

projects.name: Promoting policy engagement and programming on Governance for Resilient Futures
projects.description:
Governance for Resilient Futures is about strengthening how the machinery of government anticipates change, manages complexity, protects vulnerable groups, and adapts rapidly in times of crisis—so that national development gains are safeguarded and communities remain strong. It builds on traditional knowledge, local leadership, and the deep cultural values that have long made Pacific societies resilient.
The initiative focuses on four capability areas, each essential for building long term resilience:
1. Managing Risk Information
We help governments generate and use stronger, more holistic data on the risks shaping national futures—climate, environment, labour mobility, demographics, NCDs, social vulnerabilities, and economic pressures. This includes improving statistics, risk modelling, and future scenario development. Better information leads to better decisions.
2. Coherent, Risk Informed Policy, Planning and Delivery
We support national planning, sector strategies, budgeting systems, and local development processes to align around a unified resilience pathway. This means integrating foresight, ensuring policies consider long term risks, strengthening crisis preparedness, and helping institutions become more adaptive and agile.
3. Building a Societal Compact for Resilience
Resilience depends on whole of society action. G4RF strengthens community leadership, traditional governance structures, civil society, youth and women’s organizations, and the private sector. The aim is inclusive co design of solutions and stronger behavioural change efforts, grounded in local knowledge and values such as Te Vā and collective stewardship.
4. Securing and Managing Financing for Resilience
We help governments estimate the true cost of resilience and improve public financial management to integrate risk. We also support access to climate finance, blended finance, green taxation, diaspora mechanisms, and private sector resilience investments. The goal is sustainable, diversified financing to meet long term needs.

projects.name: Vaka Pasifika
projects.description: Vaka Pasifika (officially: “Accountable Public Finances to serve Pacific people”) is a UNDP Pacific regional governance programme (2022–2026) funded by the European Union, designed to make public finance more transparent, inclusive, and people‑centered across the Pacific. The project operates in 15 Pacific countries and territories (plus Tokelau), working with Supreme Audit Institutions, Ombuds offices, Leadership Code Commissions, Public Service Commissions, civil society (via PIANGO), and governments to strengthen oversight, improve budget planning and execution, and open fiscal decision‑making to citizen input. It builds on the earlier Strengthening Public Finance Management and Governance in the Pacific project (2018–2022) and includes flagship streams such as the Vaka Pasifika Fellowship to cultivate reform leadership and a regional eBudget platform to make budgets accessible and comparable.

projects.description: On 3 September 2024, the Vanuatu Ministry of Internal Affairs launched the country’s first National Action Plan to Combat Trafficking in Persons 2024–2028, establishing a whole-of-government and whole-of-society framework to prevent trafficking and protect vulnerable individuals. projects.name: TO10P0516 / LM0553 Strengthening Access to Regular Pathways for Labour Mobility in Tonga
projects.description: Labour mobility is central to Tonga’s economic development, and the Government’s 2020 Migration and Sustainable Development Policy seeks to maximise its benefits while managing associated risks. The proposed project supports this by strengthening governance of labour mobility through an evidence‑based, protection‑centred and gender‑sensitive Migration Profile and the establishment of a Migrant Resource Centre. Together, these efforts aim to enhance regular pathways and improve informed decision‑making for Tongan migrants.
projects.outcome: "4.3.3 Enhanced rights-based migration policy and its implementation, capacities, tools, mechanisms and initiatives on trans-boundary and migration governance and human mobility. "

projects.name: Institutional capacity of public officials and civil servants of Tokelau, strengthened through inclusive and digital governance and leadership training to effectively and responsively fulfil their roles and responsibilities.
projects.description: Development and implementation of a Governance and Leadership Training Curriculum for Tokelau. The curriculum and its modules will focus on developing the skills and knowledge of Taupulega members, civil servants, and women and youth leaders at atoll- and national- level on governance issues and leadership. Through a series of consultations, it will develop a taxonomy of definitions for governance and leadership in the Tokelau context, identify key gaps and needs, and design a series of trainingsfor officialsto enhance their ability to carry out their functions. Training courses will be developed and delivered following a comprehensive capacity and needs assessment. It will focus on, but not be limited to, issues such as ethical leadership, inclusive governance, strategic planning, gender-responsive budgeting, accounting, performance management, transparency and accountability, economic development, communication, corporate services, management processes, and prevention of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse.
projects.outcome: 4.6.3  Strengthened policies, mechanisms, and capacities to enhance opportunities for youth, women’s and people with disabilities to participate in decision-making.

children.name: First Biennial Transparency and Fourth National Communication Report (BTR1/NC4)
children.description: The enabling activity aims to assist the Cook Islands to meet its reporting requirements under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement and prepare a combined First Biennial Transparency and Fourth National Communication Report in accordance with the MPGs and methodological guidance contained in decisions 18/CMA.1 and 5/CMA.3. Additionally, to strengthen technical and institutional capacity to prepare and submit Biennial Transparency and National Communication reports to the UNFCCC. It will also assist in building national capacities to fulfil the Cook Islands commitments under the Convention on a continuous basis, whilst also increasing the awareness on climate change issues, fostering better integration of climate change into national, sectoral polices, strategies and programmes. Within the BTR1/NC4 component of the project, information will be updated on national circumstances, inventories of greenhouse gases up to 2020, measures undertaken to mitigate climate change, assessments of vulnerability to climate change and adaptation measures, and information on steps taken to integrate climate change consideration into national policies and actions.

The Smart Islands programme provides an integrated approach to enhanced access to deliver digital services to identified rural and remote communities leveraging on the four pillars of digital connectivity, affordability, digital skills and digital services. These Smart Islands programme would continue in 2024 with addition of Republic of Marshall Islands and Tuvalu.

ITU inputs: 
During the period, ITU supported (activities continue) the governments of Kiribati, F.S. Micronesia and Nauru in developing national digital transformation strategy under the SDG Fund Joint Programme. The drafts are available with the governments. Further, ITU continues to assist Fiji and Solomon Islands in developing their national digital transformation strategies.

To facilitate policy frameworks for digital infrastructure development,  ITU is providing technical assistance to Vanuatu and Tonga to develop their policies and guidelines on Universal Service Obligation and digital infrastructure sharing. Technical assistance was provided to Tonga in strengthening their Quality of Service and Quality of Experience experience of telecom services by developing national guidelines while a review of Digital TV is currently underway for Fiji. In 2024, trainings and radio seminars are also planned in 2024 to build national capacity of ITU Members in the Pacific to better manage the important digital infrastructure of frequency spectrum.

ITU inputs- Pacific Girls in ICT Day Programme was launched on 27th April 2023 together with national government, UN agencies, Pacific Islands Telecommunications Association (PITA) and Pacific Telecommunications Council (PTC). Over a period of 6 months (27 April-20 October, 2023), more than 1000 girls and young women from the Pacific raise awareness and skills through a range of activities in Fiji (275 participants, 9 trainings in Cybersecurity (Online Safety & Online Scamming), coding, emerging technologies, telecommunications, leaderships, career development); Tonga, (260 participants, 5 trainings in Cybersecurity (Online Safety), leaderships, career development and digital financial literacy); Federated States of Micronesia (40 participants, 2 trainings in Cybersecurity (Online Safety)); Nauru (12 participants, 2 trainings in Basic Cyber Safety awareness and Child online protection); Kiribati (more than 500 participants joined the awareness raising and skills development sessions in Leadership, ICT Career development, Talk Tech, Cybersecurity and Online Safety. These programmes were championed and supported by governments, UN country teams, regional organizations, civil society and academia. In addition, there were also celebrations in Papua New Guinea and Samoa. Drawing upon the success of 2023, there has been continued interests form partners to strengthen the programme further in 2024.
